title: Year 11 Chemistry Module 2 – Introduction to Quantitative Chemistry
description: A fast-recall review of NSW Year 11 Chemistry Module 2. Questions use short answers and avoid multi-step calculations or extended writing.
author: Generated with Classroom Jeopardy Quiz Maker

questions.prompt: What law states that total mass remains constant during a chemical reaction in a closed system?
questions.answer: The law of conservation of mass.

questions.prompt: What must be equal on both sides of a balanced chemical equation for each element?
What numbers placed before formulas balance a chemical equation?
What term describes the quantitative relationships between reactants and products in a reaction?
In a balanced equation, coefficients represent simple whole-number ratios of what?
What SI unit is used for amount of substance?
What constant gives the number of particles in one mole?
Approximately how many particles are in one mole?
What quantity has units of grams per mole?
What symbol is commonly used for chemical amount in moles?
What formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound?
What formula shows the actual number of each type of atom in a molecule?
What term describes the percentage by mass of each element in a compound?
What type of reactant is completely used up first and limits the amount of product formed?
questions.answer: The limiting reagent. Accept: limiting reactant.

questions.prompt: What reactant remains after the limiting reagent has been completely consumed?
questions.answer: The excess reagent. Accept: excess reactant.

questions.prompt: What substance is dissolved in a solution?

Which gas law links pressure and absolute temperature at constant volume?

questions.answer: The Ideal Gas Law. Accept: PV = nRT.
